Middleware and the Pipeline

app.use(), the order requests flow through, and why that order is never arbitrary.

Middleware is just a function with the shape (req, res, next) that Express calls on its way to handling a request. It can inspect or modify the request, send a response itself and stop there, or call next() to hand off to whatever was registered after it. app.use(someMiddleware) is how you register one.

There's no real equivalent of this in Laravel-as-you've-used-it — the closest mental model is Laravel's own middleware classes (handle($request, $next)), if you've glimpsed those: same idea, but here it's the entire framework's extension point, not one feature among many.

Looking back at Figure 1.3 (earlier this topic), app.js registers four things, in this exact order:

  1. express.json() — built-in middleware that parses a JSON request body into req.body. Laravel does this for you invisibly; Express makes it an explicit line you add.
  2. routes — the app's own routes (next slide).
  3. notFound — runs only if nothing above matched the request.
  4. errorHandler — handles any error forwarded via next(err) from anything above it.

Order matters because Express tries each registered function in registration order until one of them sends a response:

         every request
              │
              ▼
     express.json()          parses the JSON body onto req.body
              │
              ▼
         routes              tries each registered route in turn
              │
     ┌────────┴─────────┐
     │ matched          │ no route matched
     ▼                  ▼
  controller           notFound ──► 404 response

     an error thrown/rejected ANYWHERE above jumps
     straight here, skipping everything in between:
              │
              ▼
        errorHandler ──► error response

Figure 1.4 is notFound — it always sends a 404, so it must come after every real route, or it would swallow requests that should have matched one.

// Figure 1.4: catch-all for unmatched requests (src/middleware/notFound.js)
export default (req, res, next) => {
  res.status(404).json({
    error: { message: `Not found: ${req.method} ${req.originalUrl}` },
  });
};

errorHandler is last of all, for a related reason covered properly in the error-handling topic later this lesson: it needs to sit downstream of everything else so any error, from any middleware or route above it, can reach it via next(err).
